solutions.text: Scheduled water misting of haul roads and active earthwork faces, frequency set by a site wind and humidity reading
Surfactant or polymer binder sprayed on unpaved site roads (Chang 2010: about 93 % control on unpaved roads)
Covered stockpiles with windbreak netting on the upwind side
Wheel-wash and rumble grid at the site exit so trucks do not carry mud onto public roads
Enclosed on-site crushing with water spray at the crusher (Bello 2019: below the PEL with the crusher's own spray, not with a water cannon)
Wet cutting mandatory for concrete and block cutting, dry cutting banned on site (Middaugh 2012: 78 % cut)
Vacuum-shrouded saws and grinders with HEPA extraction for finishing trades
Pre-wetting of structures before demolition and during breaking
Paving or gravelling the main haul road in the first month of the project instead of the last
15 km/h site speed limit with a speed bump at the gate, which cuts road-dust lift
Perimeter dust fence whose height is set per wind direction by CFD (Choi 2023)
Fenceline PM10 sensors that trigger the perimeter misting line automatically above a threshold
Fog cannon at the fenceline aimed at the downwind boundary during dusty operations
Dense hedge or vegetation screen along the fence facing homes
Site layout that puts crushing, mixing and stockpiles at the point furthest from the neighbours' fence
FFP2 or N95 provision with fit testing for every worker in a dust trade, replaced on a schedule
Powered air-purifying respirators for cutters, chippers and grinders (Bello 2019: chipping stayed above the PEL even with N95)
Rotation cap on high-dust tasks: no worker more than 2 h a shift on cutting or breaking
Filtered, pressurised cabs for excavator and loader operators (Azarmi 2016: cabin dose 57x background for coarse particles)
Dust-task scheduling to low-wind hours from the day's forecast
Personal real-time dust badge with a vibrating alert at a set PM2.5 level (Kim 2025: alerts within 20 m)
Flexible-height barrier panels raised on the downwind side of the day (Choi 2023: resident exposure varies 2.3x with wind direction)
SMS to registered neighbours before crushing or demolition hours, advising closed windows
Demolition and crushing restricted to hours when neighbouring homes are emptiest
Wind-vane-triggered misting that runs only on the downwind boundary
Dust-operation permit tied to the forecast: no crushing, sweeping or demolition on high-wind days
Portable fog cannon repositioned daily to the neighbour side downwind
Covered skips and on-site waste separation so demolition fines do not sit in open piles
Recycled aggregate specified in the contract to cut quarry haulage and crushing on site
Silica-free abrasive and low-silica block specified for the trades that generate the finest dust
Off-site prefabrication of cut elements so cutting happens under extraction, not in the open
Midday break window aligned with the dustiest tasks so heat and dust peaks are not stacked on the same hours
Shaded rest areas with a filtered-air cabin on site
WBGT-triggered work stops with a site display of the reading
Hydration and heart-rate wearables that flag workers in the danger zone (Moohialdin 2022)
Continuous perimeter PM10 monitor with a public dashboard for the site
Truck sheeting enforced at the gate: no uncovered load leaves the site
Humidity-aware scheduling: on the most humid mornings the heaviest tasks move to the afternoon window
Site-wide dust alert on the PA or phones when any perimeter node crosses the threshold
Marked dust exclusion zones that clear non-essential workers during crushing or sweeping peaks
Contractor-funded air purifiers for the homes on the fence side for the duration of the works
Neighbour dashboard and complaint line fed by the perimeter monitors
Planning setback between the site fence and the nearest homes for future sites
Baseline and periodic spirometry for workers in high-dust trades
Silicosis surveillance register for cutters, chippers and crushers
Smoking cessation programme on site, since smoking multiplies dust harm
Medical surveillance requirement written into the visa medical for dust trades
Dust and silica training in the workers' own languages, with a short film for the site induction
Contractor dust-performance bond released against fenceline readings
Tender scoring that awards points for a measured dust plan
Public league table of sites by fenceline PM10
Drone dust patrol by the municipality over active sites on windy days
Reduced permit fees for sites that run continuous monitoring
Worker hotline for dust violations in three languages
Dust records linked to the contractor's insurance premium
Resident app to report dust clouds with a geotagged photo, routed to the site and the municipality
Dust-control competency certificate required for site supervisors
Site dust score printed as a QR on the hoarding, updated daily from the monitors
Hoarding-side realtime display of PM10 so passers-by and workers see the number
Shift-end shower and clothes-change facility so dust does not travel home
LPG conversion of charcoal grills at licensed stalls, with a rebate on the licence fee
Induction or electric grill at stalls with a power hookup
Low-smoke charcoal briquettes or coconut-shell charcoal in place of lump charcoal
Chimney starter for lighting charcoal, no lighter fluid
Power hookups installed at fixed vending spots so electric cooking is possible
Pellet grill or gas griddle for items now cooked over charcoal
Solar-battery cart powering an induction plate at outdoor markets
Canopy hood over the grill with a fan and grease filter, exhaust above head height
Extraction hood with an electrostatic precipitator on the exhaust
Water-scrubber hood for charcoal exhaust
Exhaust stack that discharges 3 m above the stall roof
Stall orientation rule: grill on the leeward edge, vendor upwind
Shared ventilated cooking kiosk at a market, several vendors under one hood
Wind wall or screen between the grill and the vendor's station
Vendor station moved to the upwind side of the grill, serving from the front
Rotation between grilling and serving so no one stands at the grill a full shift
FFP2 mask during charcoal lighting and fanning, the highest-peak minutes
Helper handles charcoal lighting and ash while wearing a respirator
Shorter charcoal shifts with a break away from the stall each hour
Clean fuel as a condition of vending licence renewal
Vendors clustered in ventilated food courts or designated zones away from traffic
Cap on charcoal stalls per street or market
Charcoal lighting restricted to set hours before the crowd arrives
Minimum spacing between grills at a market so plumes do not stack
Grill with controlled airflow and a lid so combustion is cleaner and fumes are trapped
Catalytic afterburner on the grill exhaust
Lid-on cooking for items that allow it, cutting open-flame time
Pre-cooked items finished on the grill briefly, cutting minutes over charcoal
Personal PM monitor clipped at the stall with a visible alert
Fan-based dilution blowing across the grill away from the vendor
Stall layout with the grill at the edge and the vendor inside a partly enclosed counter
Customer queue positioned upwind of the grill so the crowd is not in the plume
Respiratory symptom screening at licence renewal with referral
Vendor health survey and free lung-function check at a market
Training session for vendors on smoke exposure and the cheap fixes
CO alarm at charcoal stalls in semi-enclosed spots
Clean-stall label displayed to customers, awarded after a measurement
Municipality rebate for hood installation at licensed stalls
Vendor cooperative bulk-buying LPG and cylinders
Air-quality display facing customers at the stall
Event-organiser rule: electric hookups and no charcoal at organised markets and festivals
Hood retrofit built and installed by the engineering student group at one market as the pilot
Filter-cleaning subscription so hoods keep working after installation
Measurement campaign ranking stall types by PM2.5 so the worst are fixed first
Trained smoke marshal at markets who checks fuel, hoods and spacing
Clean cooking zone pilot at one market with LPG and hoods for every stall
Nose-and-mouth shield at the grill face for the minutes of flare-up
Enclosed food truck with roof extraction and filter instead of an open stall
Vendor spacing and orientation drawn into the market floor plan
Two-station stall: hot station for 20 minutes, cold station for 20, alternating
School idle-free policy with signage at the gate and in the parent handbook
Engine-off pledge signed by parents and drivers at the start of term
Staff-enforced engine-off in the queue with a verbal reminder at the window (Ryan 2013: 4.11 to 0.99 ug/m3 at the most-bused school)
Student idle marshals with tally sheets at the gate
Camera plus plate reading that sends a letter home to idling families
Idle-free zone painted on the road surface at the drop-off
Municipal anti-idling rule for school zones with an air-quality rationale (Abu Dhabi Police's Dh300 covers unattended engines only)
Countdown display at the gate showing minutes since arrival, engine-off asked at one minute
Engine-off training for hired family drivers, who do most Abu Dhabi school runs

Park-and-stride: drop-off point 300 m away with a marshalled walking route
Staggered drop-off and pick-up by grade to shorten the queue
One-way rolling drop-off loop, no stopping, staff open the doors
Drop-off bays relocated away from the pedestrian gate
Kiss-and-ride lane with attendants so cars keep moving
Pedestrian entrance moved to the side away from the queue
Shaded, cooled parent waiting area so parents do not wait in cars with the AC on
Covered walkway from the drop-off bay to the door
Hedge or tree screen between the queue lane and the gate

Numbered pick-up tags and a call board, the low-tech version of the app (car half only, rescored 04:10 with the app)
Remote pick-up points at a nearby car park with staff walking the children over
Walking bus with adult marshals from a collection point
Portable HEPA cleaners in classrooms (Simona 2025: PM2.5 39.9 % lower over the year)
MERV13 filter upgrade on the school's air handling units
Positive pressure in gate-side classrooms with filtered supply air
Sealing window and door gaps on the gate-facing façade
Purifiers only in the gate-facing classrooms, the cheapest targeting
Filter change schedule driven by a classroom PM sensor
Siting rule for new schools: at least 300 m from an arterial
Gate placement rule away from the arterial for new schools
Room allocation: the youngest classes furthest from the gate and the road
Automatic idle shut-off timers on school buses
Electric school buses on the routes serving the school
Shore power at the depot and the staging area so bus AC runs without the engine
Bus staging area away from the gate, engines off until loading
Bus arrival slots so buses load on arrival instead of waiting
Diesel oxidation catalyst or DPF retrofit on older buses
Telematics idle report per bus with a league table for the operator
Driver bonus for the lowest idle hours
CNG buses on school contracts
Demand-controlled ventilation with CO2 and PM sensors (Arar 2021: ventilation beat purifiers in UAE nurseries)
Outdoor-air intake reduced during the drop-off peak, restored after
Air intake relocated away from the gate and the road
Energy recovery ventilator with filtration for the gate-side wing
School bus fee discount funded by a car drop-off fee
Carpool matching for families on the same streets
Enrolment preference for families within walking distance
Bike and e-scooter parking with a safe entry lane
Public bus route stop at the school gate at the school's hours
Staff load and unload children so the queue rolls (Kumar 2020: drop-off PM2.5 nearly 3x off-peak from queuing)
No-parking, roll-through rule with cones and a marshal
Parent briefing on engine-off in the queue at the term's first assembly
Signage that states the fuel and dirhams saved by switching off
Physical distance: the queue lane moved 30 m from the pedestrian gate
Enclosed, ventilated gate vestibule where children wait
Green wall at the gate as a partial screen (Kumar 2024: hedges about 23 %)
Stable-morning alert: on inversion days the queue is shortened by a later staggered slot
Dust and inversion day protocol: children wait indoors at pick-up
Windows closed during drop-off and pick-up in gate-side rooms
Gate-side doors kept shut during the peak, entry through the far door
Air curtain at the main entrance
No chalk, wet cleaning and HEPA vacuums after hours (Arar 2021: TSP moved with children's activity)
Entrance mats and a shoe-off rule in the youngest classes
No incense or air fresheners in classrooms
Black-carbon co-benefit reported in the school's sustainability report
Youngest pupils kept away from the tail of the queue at pick-up
Real-time PM display at the gate visible to every parent in the queue
Weekly gate air-quality report to parents
ADEK guideline for school-gate air, drafted from the pilot's data
Air quality as a criterion in the school inspection framework
Student measurement project with low-cost sensors feeding the gate display
Class competition on engine-off rates counted by the marshals
Peak-hour parking enforcement on the gate road by the municipality
Fee rebate for families who use the bus all year
Clean-commute badge for families who walk, bus or carpool
Corridor doors kept shut on the gate side to keep the peak out of the wing
Bus AC pre-cooled on shore power before departure so the wait at the gate is engine-off
Queue lane on the downwind side of the gate on the prevailing wind

Gate orchestration system: buses get arrival slots and an engine-off staging bay, cars get the just-in-time call, one dashboard at the door (rescored 04:10 after the pre-mortem: engine-off is not available in the heat, the wait relocates, the gate effect is under sensor noise)

Electric buses required in the next school transport tender
Route optimisation to cut time on board for the youngest pupils

HEPA-grade cabin filters on the school buses
Cabin PM monitor on each bus with driver feedback

Asthma-register pupils get a personal alert on dust and peak days
Outdoor PE timetable set by the forecast
School-level air-quality display in the lobby
Parent app showing commute air quality by route
Route advice: walking routes on quieter streets, away from the queue
School nurse asthma action plans for every registered pupil
Inhaler-at-school programme
Spirometry screening for the highest-exposure pupils
DPF or DOC retrofit on the oldest buses (Adar 2015: on-board particles 10 to 50 % lower with cleaner tech)
Closed crankcase ventilation retrofit, the cheapest cabin fix
Bus age cap in the school's transport contract
Electric buses on the longest routes first
Positive-pressure filtered cabin on the buses
Seating plan: youngest at the front, away from the engine and exhaust

Idle timers on buses so cabin fumes do not build while waiting
